subject: maths
title: Year 5 Estimation and Money Problems
seo_title: Year 5 Estimation and Money Worksheets: Free Maths with Answer Key (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Check and explain the reasonableness of solutions to problems including financial contexts using estimation strategies appropriate to the context
meta_desc: Free Year 5 maths worksheets on estimation and money, aligned to the Australian Curriculum (AC9M5N08, AC9M5N09): round to estimate, front-end estimation, check if answers are reasonable, round prices to the nearest dollar, round cash to the nearest 5c, and solve budget and best-buy problems. 100 questions with an answer key, great for NAPLAN practice.
key_big: Estimate first, then check: if 412 × 9 gives 37 080 but 400 × 9 = 3600, the answer is not reasonable.
key_sub: Round prices to the nearest dollar to estimate a total. When you pay cash, round the total to the nearest 5c first: $8.62 becomes $8.60, so the change from $10 is $1.40.
body_html:
Estimate first, then check

An estimate is a quick answer that is close to the exact answer. Round the numbers to friendly numbers, then work out the estimate in your head. If your exact answer is far from the estimate, check your working.

Way to estimate4682 + 2371Estimate
Round to the nearest 10005000 + 20007000
Round to the nearest 1004700 + 24007100
Front-end: keep the first digit4000 + 20006000

The exact answer is 7053. Rounding to the nearest 100 gives the closest estimate. Front-end estimation is the quickest, but its answer is always lower than the exact answer.

Is the answer reasonable?

Noah says 412 × 9 = 37 080.

Estimate: 400 × 9 = 3600. 37 080 is about 10 times too big, so it is not reasonable. The exact answer is 3708.

Answer: not reasonable

Estimating with money

Round each price to the nearest dollar. 50c or more rounds up; less than 50c rounds down.

Will $50 be enough?

A school bag costs $29.95, a hat $12.40 and a ruler $2.60.

Round: $30 + $12 + $3 = $45. $45 is less than $50, so $50 is enough.

Answer: yes

Paying cash: round to the nearest 5c

Australia has no 1c or 2c coins. When you pay with cash, the total is rounded to the nearest 5c. If you pay by card, you pay the exact amount.

Cash change

The bill is $8.62. You pay cash with a $10 note.

Round the total first: $8.62 → $8.60. Then $10 − $8.60 = $1.40.

Answer: $1.40

Compare deals

Juice boxes cost $1.40 each, or 4 for $5.

4 × $1.40 = $5.60. $5.60 − $5.00 = 60c, so the 4 for $5 deal saves 60c.

Answer: 4 for $5

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Rounding $3.65 down to $365c is more than 50c, so round up: $4
Estimating 400 × 9 as 36 000Count the zeros: 4 hundreds × 9 = 36 hundreds = 3600
Writing 407c as $4.70 or $40.70100c = $1, so 407c = $4.07
Forgetting to round a cash total: $10 − $8.62 = $1.38Round first: $8.60, so the change is $1.40
Choosing the deal with the smaller price tagCompare the same amount: the price for 1 litre, or for 3 items

faq.q: What does Year 5 learn about estimation in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: Year 5 students check and explain whether answers are reasonable by estimating, including in money problems (AC9M5N08). They round numbers, use front-end estimation and compare the estimate with the exact answer.
Keep the first digit of each number and make the other digits 0, then calculate. For 6815 + 2742 the estimate is 6000 + 2000 = 8000; it is quick but always lower than the exact answer (here 9557).

faq.q: How does rounding to the nearest 5 cents work in Australia?
faq.a: Cash totals are rounded because there are no 1c or 2c coins. Totals ending in 1 or 2 round down to 0, 3 or 4 round up to 5, 6 or 7 round down to 5, and 8 or 9 round up to 10. Card payments are not rounded.

faq.q: How can my child check if an answer is reasonable?
faq.a: Round the numbers, work out an estimate in your head and compare. If 412 × 9 gives 37 080 but 400 × 9 = 3600, the answer is too big and should be checked.

items.q: Round 368 to the nearest 10.
items.e: 368 is between 360 and 370. Look at the ones digit: 8. 5 or more, so round up to 370.

items.q: Round 7451 to the nearest 100.
items.e: 7451 is between 7400 and 7500. Look at the tens digit: 5. 5 or more, so round up to 7500.

items.q: Round 4682 to the nearest 1000.
items.e: 4682 is between 4000 and 5000. Look at the hundreds digit: 6. 5 or more, so round up to 5000.

items.q: Round 2507 to the nearest 1000.
items.e: 2507 is between 2000 and 3000. Look at the hundreds digit: 5. 5 or more, so round up to 3000.

items.q: Estimate 63 + 28 by rounding each number to the nearest 10.
items.e: 63 rounds to 60 and 28 rounds to 30. 60 + 30 = 90. (The exact answer is 91.)

items.q: Estimate 94 − 47 by rounding each number to the nearest 10.
items.e: 94 rounds to 90 and 47 rounds to 50. 90 − 50 = 40. (The exact answer is 47.)

items.q: Estimate 347 + 486 by rounding each number to the nearest 100.
items.e: 347 rounds to 300 and 486 rounds to 500. 300 + 500 = 800. (The exact answer is 833.)

items.q: Estimate 812 − 385 by rounding each number to the nearest 100.
items.e: 812 rounds to 800 and 385 rounds to 400. 800 − 400 = 400. (The exact answer is 427.)

items.q: Estimate 629 + 254 by rounding each number to the nearest 100.
items.e: 629 rounds to 600 and 254 rounds to 300. 600 + 300 = 900. (The exact answer is 883.)

items.e: 935 rounds to 900 and 468 rounds to 500. 900 − 500 = 400. (The exact answer is 467.)

items.q: Estimate 4682 + 2371 by rounding each number to the nearest 1000.
items.e: 4682 rounds to 5000 and 2371 rounds to 2000. 5000 + 2000 = 7000. (The exact answer is 7053.)

items.q: Estimate 8350 − 2716 by rounding each number to the nearest 1000.
items.e: 8350 rounds to 8000 and 2716 rounds to 3000. 8000 − 3000 = 5000. (The exact answer is 5634.)

items.q: Estimate 3529 + 4475 by rounding each number to the nearest 1000.
items.e: 3529 rounds to 4000 and 4475 rounds to 4000. 4000 + 4000 = 8000. (The exact answer is 8004.)

items.q: Estimate 9208 − 4861 by rounding each number to the nearest 1000.
items.e: 9208 rounds to 9000 and 4861 rounds to 5000. 9000 − 5000 = 4000. (The exact answer is 4347.)

items.q: Estimate 6 × 38 by rounding 38 to the nearest 10.
items.e: 38 rounds to 40. 6 × 40 = 240. (The exact answer is 228.)

items.q: Estimate 7 × 293 by rounding 293 to the nearest 100.
items.e: 293 rounds to 300. 7 × 300 = 2100. (The exact answer is 2051.)

items.q: Use front-end estimation to estimate 6815 + 2742.
items.e: Keep the first digit of each number and make the other digits 0: 6000 + 2000 = 8000. (The exact answer is 9557.)

items.q: Use front-end estimation to estimate 538 + 376.
items.e: Keep the first digit of each number and make the other digits 0: 500 + 300 = 800. (The exact answer is 914.)

items.q: Use front-end estimation to estimate 7384 − 2915.
items.e: Keep the first digit of each number and make the other digits 0: 7000 − 2000 = 5000. (The exact answer is 4469.)

items.q: Use front-end estimation to estimate 4 × 1873.
items.e: Keep the first digit of 1873 and make the other digits 0: 1000. 4 × 1000 = 4000. (The exact answer is 7492. A front-end estimate is always lower than the exact answer.)

items.q: Ruby works out 308 × 6 and gets 18 480. Estimate to check. Is the answer reasonable?
items.e: Estimate: 300 × 6 = 1800. 18 480 is not close to 1800, so it is not reasonable. The exact answer is 1848.

items.e: Estimate: 5000 + 3000 = 8000. 8165 is close to 8000, so it is reasonable.

items.e: Estimate: 25 × 40 = 1000. 125 is not close to 1000, so it is not reasonable. The exact answer is 1025.

items.q: Which estimate is closest to the exact answer of 498 × 6?
items.e: 500 × 6 = 3000. (The exact answer is 2988, so this estimate is the closest.)

items.q: Which estimate is closest to the exact answer of 3125 ÷ 5?
items.e: 3000 ÷ 5 = 600. (The exact answer is 625, so this estimate is the closest.)

items.q: Which estimate is closest to the exact answer of 6890 + 2155?
items.e: 7000 + 2000 = 9000. (The exact answer is 9045, so this estimate is the closest.)

items.q: Which estimate is closest to the exact answer of 8 × 3976?
items.e: 8 × 4000 = 32 000. (The exact answer is 31 808, so this estimate is the closest.)

items.q: A glue stick costs $3.45. What is the price to the nearest dollar?
items.e: $3.45 is between $3 and $4. Look at the cents: 45c is less than 50c, so round down to $3.

items.q: A pair of thongs costs $7.50. What is the price to the nearest dollar?
items.e: $7.50 is exactly halfway between $7 and $8. Halfway rounds up, so $8.

items.q: A beach towel costs $12.95. What is the price to the nearest dollar?
items.e: $12.95 is between $12 and $13. Look at the cents: 95c is more than 50c, so round up to $13.

items.q: A notebook costs $4.08. What is the price to the nearest dollar?
items.e: $4.08 is between $4 and $5. Look at the cents: 8c is less than 50c, so round down to $4.

items.q: A pencil costs 85c. What is the price to the nearest dollar?
items.e: 85c is between 0c and $1. Look at the cents: 85c is more than 50c, so round up to $1.

items.q: A cricket ball costs $19.62. What is the price to the nearest dollar?
items.e: $19.62 is between $19 and $20. Look at the cents: 62c is more than 50c, so round up to $20.

items.q: Round each price to the nearest dollar. Estimate the total cost.
items.e: Round each price to the nearest dollar: $3 + $4 + $2 = $9. (The exact total is $8.80.)

items.q: Round each price to the nearest dollar. Estimate the total cost.
items.e: Round each price to the nearest dollar: $17 + $12 + $6 + $4 = $39. (The exact total is $39.30.)

items.q: Mia has $50 at the shops. She wants to buy a lunch box for $12.95, a drink bottle for $18.40 and a pencil case for $9.60. Is $50 enough? Estimate to decide.
items.e: Round to the nearest dollar: $13 + $18 + $10 = $41. $41 is less than $50, so yes, it is enough. (The exact total is $40.95.)

items.q: Chloe has $20 at the book fair. She wants to buy a novel for $14.99 and a colouring book for $8.25. Is $20 enough? Estimate to decide.
items.e: Round to the nearest dollar: $15 + $8 = $23. $23 is more than $20, so no, it is not enough. (The exact total is $23.24.)

items.q: Grace has $50 at the toy shop. She wants to buy a kite for $23.50, a frisbee for $11.80 and a ball for $9.75. Is $50 enough? Estimate to decide.
items.e: Round to the nearest dollar: $24 + $12 + $10 = $46. $46 is less than $50, so yes, it is enough. (The exact total is $45.05.)

items.q: Jack has $10 at the athletics carnival. He wants to buy a hot dog for $6.50, a juice for $3.80 and an ice block for $2.90. Is $10 enough? Estimate to decide.
items.e: Round to the nearest dollar: $7 + $4 + $3 = $14. $14 is more than $10, so no, it is not enough. (The exact total is $13.20.)

items.q: Harper has $50 at the surf shop. She wants to buy a T-shirt for $19.90, shorts for $22.45 and goggles for $14.60. Is $50 enough? Estimate to decide.
items.e: Round to the nearest dollar: $20 + $22 + $15 = $57. $57 is more than $50, so no, it is not enough. (The exact total is $56.95.)

items.q: Noah buys 4 packets of stickers at $2.95 each. Round the price to the nearest dollar. About how much does he spend?
items.e: $2.95 rounds to $3. 4 × $3 = $12. (The exact cost is $11.80.)

items.q: Movie tickets cost $6.20 each. About how much do 3 tickets cost?
items.e: $6.20 rounds to $6. 3 × $6 = $18. (The exact cost is $18.60.)

items.q: Mum pays for these with a $20 note. About how much change does she get?
Dad buys a cricket ball for $19.60, batting gloves for $23.10 and a cap for $8.40. He pays with a $100 note. About how much change does he get?
Write 407c in dollars.
items.e: 100c = $1. 407c = 400c + 7c = $4 and 7c = $4.07. The cents always take two digits.

items.q: Write $2.60 in cents.

items.e: Count on from $6.35: to the next dollar, then to $10. 65c + $3 = $3.65.
Count on from $12.85: to the next dollar, then to $20. 15c + $7 = $7.15.
Count on from $37.40: to the next dollar, then to $50. 60c + $12 = $12.60.

items.q: What is 3 × $2.45?
What is 4 × $3.80?
Share $7.50 equally between 3 people. How much does each person get?
Share $9.60 equally between 4 people. How much does each person get?
A shop rounds cash totals to the nearest 5c. What does a $4.37 bill cost in cash?
items.e: Look at the last digit of the cents: 7 rounds down to 5. $4.37 is closer to $4.35 than to $4.40, so the cash total is $4.35.

items.q: A shop rounds cash totals to the nearest 5c. What does a $6.91 bill cost in cash?
items.e: Look at the last digit of the cents: 1 rounds down to 0. $6.91 is closer to $6.90 than to $6.95, so the cash total is $6.90.

items.q: A shop rounds cash totals to the nearest 5c. What does a $3.48 bill cost in cash?
items.e: Look at the last digit of the cents: 8 rounds up to 10. $3.48 is closer to $3.50 than to $3.45, so the cash total is $3.50.

items.q: A shop rounds cash totals to the nearest 5c. What does a $12.93 bill cost in cash?
items.e: Look at the last digit of the cents: 3 rounds up to 5. $12.93 is closer to $12.95 than to $12.90, so the cash total is $12.95.

items.q: The bill is $6.42. You pay cash with a $10 note, and the total is rounded to the nearest 5c. How much change do you get?
items.e: First round the total to the nearest 5c: $6.42 → $6.40. Then $10 − $6.40 = $3.60.

items.q: The bill is $13.47. You pay cash with a $20 note, and the total is rounded to the nearest 5c. How much change do you get?
items.e: First round the total to the nearest 5c: $13.47 → $13.45. Then $20 − $13.45 = $6.55.

items.q: The bill is $27.68. You pay cash with a $50 note, and the total is rounded to the nearest 5c. How much change do you get?
items.e: First round the total to the nearest 5c: $27.68 → $27.70. Then $50 − $27.70 = $22.30.

items.q: The bill is $4.19. You pay cash with a $5 note, and the total is rounded to the nearest 5c. How much change do you get?
items.e: First round the total to the nearest 5c: $4.19 → $4.20. Then $5 − $4.20 = 80c.

items.q: A class of 28 students goes on a school excursion to the zoo. Entry is $12 for each student. What is the total entry cost?
The bus for a school excursion costs $450. The cost is shared equally by 25 students. How much does each student pay?
A group of 31 students goes to the aquarium. Each ticket costs $19. Round both numbers to estimate the total cost.
items.e: 31 rounds to 30 and $19 rounds to $20. 30 × $20 = $600. (The exact cost is $589.)

items.q: At the sausage sizzle, a sausage in bread costs $3.50. Lachlan buys 4 for his family. How much does he pay?
Ethan saves $6 of his pocket money every week. He wants a skateboard that costs $75. How many weeks does he need to save?
items.e: $75 ÷ $6 = 12 remainder $3. After 12 weeks he has $72, which is not enough, so he needs 13 weeks.

items.q: Aarav gets $8 pocket money each week and saves half of it. How much does he save in 6 weeks?
Muesli bars cost $1.80 each, or 3 for $5. How much do you save if you buy the 3 for $5 deal?
A 2 L bottle of milk costs $3.20. A 1 L bottle costs $1.75. Which is the better buy?
c: the 1 L bottle: it costs less
items.e: Compare the price of 1 litre. $3.20 ÷ 2 = $1.60 per litre, which is less than $1.75, so the 2 L bottle is the better buy.

items.q: At the school canteen Charlotte buys a sushi roll for $4.20 and a juice for $2.50. She pays with a $10 note. How much change does she get?
items.e: $4.20 + $2.50 = $6.70. $10 − $6.70 = $3.30. (The total ends in 0, so no rounding is needed.)

items.q: The shopping costs $23.47. Mum pays cash with a $50 note, so the total is rounded to the nearest 5c. How much change does she get?
Leo’s bill is $9.98. He pays in cash, so the total is rounded to the nearest 5c. How much does he pay?
items.e: The last digit is 8, and 8 rounds up to 10. $9.98 → $10.00.

items.q: Year 5 sells 46 cupcakes at $2.50 each for a fundraiser. How much money do they raise?
Matilda buys 6 packs of footy cards at $4.95 each. The screen shows $297.00. Is this reasonable?
items.e: $4.95 rounds to $5. 6 × $5 = $30, so $297.00 is not reasonable. The exact total is $29.70; the point was put in the wrong place.

items.q: Year 5 has $900 for an excursion. The bus costs $350, and entry is $8 for each of the 62 students. How much money is left?
Isla saves $4.85 every week for 10 weeks. Round to the nearest dollar. About how much does she save?
items.e: $4.85 rounds to $5. 10 × $5 = $50. (The exact amount is $48.50.)

items.q: Apples cost $4.90 per kilogram and bananas cost $3.50 per kilogram. Dad buys 2 kg of apples and 3 kg of bananas. How much does he pay?
Pens cost $1.20 each, or $9.50 for a pack of 10. How much do you save if you buy the pack?
After the swimming carnival, 4 friends share a $34.80 pizza bill equally. How much does each pay?
Sienna has $20. She wants a footy for $14.95 and socks for $5.50. Estimate. Does she have enough?
items.e: Round: $15 + $6 = $21. $21 is more than $20, so no. (The exact total is $20.45.)

items.q: Pool entry costs $4.50 for one visit, or $13 for a 3-visit pass. Ava goes 3 times. Which is cheaper, and by how much?
